scope: Primary-source review of continuous-treatment nonlinear marginal effects, heterogeneity and threshold inference. No model fitting, installation or old test reopening.

sources.title: Doubly Robust Inference on Causal Derivative Effects for Continuous Treatments
sources.status: arXiv preprint; v2 2025-04-18; author publications page still lists it under Preprints; no formal journal publication verified
sources.replication_repository_license: No separate explicit license verified; use the MIT package source for permitted reuse
sources.decision: Best matched new use: estimate marginal compensation effect directly. First do a formula microcheck; retain existing DR curve as current main method.
sources.fit: Targets derivative of population causal mean under identification/smoothness/support assumptions. Conditional effect modification does not identify causal effects of the conditioning variables themselves.
sources.positivity_exception: The without-positivity branch adds an additive structural outcome assumption; it cannot generally accommodate arbitrary compensation-by-state interactions or recover unsupported heterogeneous curves.
sources.implementation_cost: Low for independent CPU formula with supplied nuisance values; medium with cross-fitted spline/Ridge nuisance learning. Author package imports torch even for sklearn branch. No package was installed.

sources.title: Causal Inference with a Continuous Treatment: Addressing Positivity Constraints, Nonlinearity, and Effect Heterogeneity
sources.license_and_maintenance: Replication entrance verified; package license and version not independently inspected, no code reused
sources.contribution: Explains how nonlinear dose response and pretreatment effect heterogeneity can be observationally indistinguishable when treatment ranges differ strongly across groups. Small additive-shift targets can require less extrapolation.
sources.decision: Use its identification lesson and same-observations/different-counterfactual example. A local shift is an optional additional estimand, not a replacement of the user's required continuous amount curve.

sources.title: Parameterizing the effect of a continuous treatment using average derivative effects
sources.contribution: Efficient density-free estimators for weighted scalar average derivative effects using Riesz representations and local overlap. The estimand generally differs from an unweighted population derivative curve.
sources.decision: Reserve for a compact sensitivity summary when a weighted scalar target is substantively useful; does not provide the required whole curve or its local threshold.
sources.cost: Author R research code with mgcv/ranger/SuperLearner and other dependencies; medium-high integration cost relative to formula microcheck

sources.title: Debiased inference for a covariate-adjusted regression function
sources.license: Unresolved: DESCRIPTION retains literal template use_mit_license(), use_gpl3_license() or friends to pick a license; no explicit top-level license verified. Do not describe repository as MIT/GPL or copy its code without clarification.
sources.contribution: Explicit local-polynomial smoothing-bias correction for a covariate-adjusted mean curve, with pointwise/difference and uniform-band inference under stated conditions, avoiding undersmoothing.
sources.decision: Strong later candidate for principled whole-curve and level-set threshold inference. Independently implementing paper mathematics is possible; current conditional multiplier bands do not already constitute this method.
sources.cost: R package depends on nprobust/SuperLearner and several learners. Medium-high for full reproduction, no installation attempted.

sources.title: Data-Driven Uniform Inference for General Continuous Treatment Models via Minimum-Variance Weighting
sources.author_code: No author repository independently verified at paper entrance
sources.license_and_maintenance: No reusable code license or maintenance record verified
sources.contribution: Minimum-variance balancing weights with a closed-form sieve solution, local-linear generalized dose-response estimation, bootstrap uniform bands and bias-control tuning.
sources.decision: Reserve alternative; it is not a new DR uniform estimator. Its Section 2 explicitly leaves doubly robust GDRF/uniform inference to future work. Higher independent reproduction cost; do not transplant its guarantee onto current DR.

sources.title: Debiased inference for proximal dose-response function
sources.fit: Targets dose-response and first derivative under unmeasured confounding using distinct treatment-/outcome-inducing proxies and bridge functions, with explicit smoothing-bias correction.
sources.decision: Not first implementation: current EV schema has no validated pair of proximal proxies. Current I/P channels or Y>0 cannot simply be declared suitable proxies. Relevant only if the needed variables and identification assumptions become defensible.

direct_derivative_formula.source: Zhang-Chen Eq(8), Remarks 3-4 and Appendix A.2
direct_derivative_formula.notation: A_i observed amount; a query amount; m(a,X)=E[Y|A=a,X]; beta(a,X)=partial_a m(a,X); p(A_i|X_i) density at observed amount; z_i=(A_i-a)/h; kappa2=integral u^2 K(u)du
direct_derivative_formula.estimate: mean_i q_i(a), cross-fitted auxiliary values when estimated
direct_derivative_formula.kernel: Paper A5 assumes bounded compact support [-1,1]. Epanechnikov .75*(1-u^2)*I(|u|<=1), kappa2=1/5; author pinned rbf.py lines48-65 and251-252 agree. Gaussian algebra has kappa2=1 but is not literally the stated compact-support condition.
direct_derivative_formula.self_normalization: Author self_norm divides only residual correction term by c(a)=mean[K((A-a)/h)/(h*p(A|X))]; beta term remains unnormalized. Non-self-normalized Eq8 is the clearest initial formula check.
direct_derivative_formula.trimming: Author tau replaces density estimates below tau by tau, not row deletion. This changes finite-sample formula; no silent clipping needed in an oracle positive-density microcheck.
direct_derivative_formula.inference: DR function returns estimate and pointwise sd. Paper Remark4 uses one common multiplier per observation across all query values. Repeated-user adaptation requires user grouping/shared user multipliers and its own validation; it is not automatically the paper's iid theorem.

static_author_code_findings.finding: t_new depends on whole query grid; beta_hat/beta_can use np.diff(predictions) without division by np.diff(t_new). For m(a)=a this returns grid spacing rather than derivative 1; query insertion also changes the approximation.
static_author_code_findings.status: Static source/formula discrepancy; not a full author performance benchmark. Do not exploit incorrect baseline to claim improvement.

static_author_code_findings.finding: Gradient written to beta_hat[j,i] but subsequently read via beta_hat[te_ind,i]; global fold indices and local j are inconsistent.
static_author_code_findings.status: Static indexing discrepancy; no neural model executed.

static_author_code_findings.finding: Uses an n-by-m independent multiplier matrix in the RA-only branch. This is not a ready implementation of the DR simultaneous process with one shared multiplier per observation across queries.
static_author_code_findings.status: Do not present this helper as validated DR uniform inference.

minimal_next_check.decision: Independent no-fit numerical Eq8 check with supplied m, beta and positive density; no old cohort reuse and no method replacement
checks: Interior compact-kernel integral agrees with independent scalar summation and analytical derivative on smooth bounded-response mechanisms
Linear/zero derivative, nonlinear saturation and sign-changing derivative examples; changing query grid leaves existing queries identical
Same-observations/different-counterfactual nonoverlap example demonstrates when nonlinear population curve and heterogeneous group curves are not identified

If nuisance fitting is later authorized, share existing spline Ridge/GPS/user folds and compare derivative error with current smoothed derivative; evaluate on new cohorts with explicit derivative truth
minimal_next_check.does_not_establish: Empirical superiority, full uniform inference, real EV causal mechanism, multi-factor graph recovery or successful identification without support
